# EPIGRAM ON THE PHILOSOPHERS’ STONE, BY ALEXANDER <note>original: "Alex:" referring to Alexander von Süchten (c. 1520–1575), a chemist and physician whose work focused on the "mercury of the philosophers."</note>
## By Alexander von Süchten to Guillaume Blanc <note>Guillaume Blanc was a 16th-century scholar and translator known for his interest in Hermetic philosophy.</note>

*We dissolve the living Body with Apolline fire <note>original: "Apollineo igne." In alchemy, Apollo represents the Sun, signifying a specific, constant heat used to break down substances.</note>,*
*So that what was previously a STONE may become Spirit.*
*And from its innermost secret chambers we draw forth*
->GOLD,<-
*Which washes its sickly face from the mother’s filth;*
*After the Bones have joined themselves with the birth-seed,*
*We then wash them with this kindred water.*
*Born from these, clothed in various colors,*
*Is a BIRD <note>original: "Ales." In alchemical imagery, a "bird" or "winged creature" represents the volatile state of matter—substances that rise as vapor when heated.</note>, which flies into heaven once it has become White.*
*Then we paint its wings with a new Fire,*
*And soak them, colored with its own milk:*
*And that which remains, we feed to it with Blood,*
*Until, fully grown, it can endure the rage of Mulciber <note>original: "Mulciber," an epithet for Vulcan, the Roman god of fire; here it represents the intense, transformative heat of the furnace.</note>.*
*Thrice-Greatest*
->HERMES<-
*called this Bird his own, William, and it has no equal in all the world.*

->B. F. V. F. P. L. C. T. T. P. M. E.<-
<note>These initials represent the formal titles and honors of the editor, Benedict Figulus (Benedictus Figulus Utenhovensis, Poeta Laureatus Caesareus, etc.).</note>

*That this Blessed BIRD may be born in our garden,*
*Long desired; O kind Christ, grant your favor.*

<summary>A dedication poem by Alexander von Süchten that uses the metaphor of a "winged bird" to describe the volatile stages of the alchemical Great Work. It concludes with a prayer for success in the laboratory through the favor of Christ.</summary>
<keywords>Alexander von Süchten, Guillaume Blanc, Hermes Trismegistus, alchemical bird, sublimation, gold, Apolline fire, Benedict Figulus</keywords>

Various *opinions* <note>original: "opinionibus"</note>, views, delusions, and erroneous thoughts of the ancient Pagans (who were once held to be wise people), which were accepted as the Truth and are still tenaciously <note>original: "mordicus"</note> and impudently defended today: For they arise from an unfavorable heaven and constellation, evil influences, and also from the *inspirations of Satan* <note>original: "Inspirationibus Sathanae"</note>; and at that time were regarded as great secrets and sanctuaries, just as they are still esteemed by the majority of the learned: though it is actually an erroneous, false, deadly, and seductive wisdom which comes to nothing with the body in the grave, becoming dust and ashes. And this is the very thing against which the holy, highly-enlightened Apostle Paul warns us in his Epistle: *“Beware of empty philosophy”* <note>original: "Cavete vobis ab inani Philosophia"</note>, and see to it that you are not led astray by false philosophies.

This *philosophy*—although it was earnestly and diligently inculcated <note>original: "inculcirt," meaning to be persistently taught or pressed in</note> and forced upon me in the schools from my youth, as unfortunately still happens to others today—nevertheless, through the special inspiration of the Holy Spirit, it has always been *suspicious* <note>original: "suspect"</note> and...

...could reasonably be preferred, since he learned the investigation of nature better from the stars and created things than our puffed-up, know-it-all philosophers today attempt to teach others, while they themselves fundamentally understand nothing.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;But this, our Hermetic Philosophy—which encompasses within itself the true astronomy, alchemy, and magic, as well as the Cabala, etc.—is an ancient, true, and natural science <term>Scientia; the Latin term for a systematic body of knowledge</term> originating from Adam. He possessed complete knowledge in all things both before and after the Fall, which was then inherited and left behind from one person to another among the Patriarchs <note>original: "Altvätter"; the biblical ancestors such as Noah, Abraham, and Enoch</note> and the dear friends of God. 

After the Great Flood <note>original: "Sündfluß"</note>, this universal knowledge and science of true natural philosophy—which had sprung forth within them from the bright Light of Nature—was divided piece by piece and distributed into different places and regions. It was also scattered <note>original: "spargirt"; a Germanized version of the Latin *spargere*, meaning to sprinkle or disperse</note> and its power was greatly weakened and diminished, so that from this separation a state of "partiality" arose: one man became an astronomer <term>Astronomus</term>, another a mage <term>Magus</term>, a third a Cabalist <term>Cabalist</term>, and a fourth an alchemist <term>Alchymist</term>.

# XVII. PROPOSITIONS BY WHICH
### *it is clearly demonstrated: What a Physician is, what his Medicine is, and also by what Remedies illnesses are expelled from human bodies.*

---

<margin>1</margin> Illnesses, of whatever kind they may be, take their origin from one of the principal organs <note>In the medical tradition of this time, the "principal organs" (*membra principalia*) usually referred to the heart, brain, liver, and sometimes the lungs or kidneys.</note>, or lie hidden within one of them.

<margin>2</margin> Illnesses cannot be expelled except through the generation of good blood in that very organ in which the illness resides.

<margin>3</margin> Good blood is generated from nourishment through the digestive heat of the ailing organ.

<margin>4</margin> Through illness, the natural heat is hindered from digesting nourishment.

<margin>5</margin> Unless nourishment is digested, blood is not generated.

<margin>6</margin> The natural heat by which every thing is digested for the sustenance and multiplication of individuals is the heat of the Sun and the Moon. <note>In Paracelsian medicine, the "Sun" and "Moon" represent universal vital principles (often linked to Sulfur and Mercury) that exist both in the sky and within the human body.</note>

Preservative medicines, however, ought to be extremely durable and far removed from corruption; for since they must preserve the human Body from corruption, it is essential that they themselves be durable first. # ALEXANDER VON SUCHTEN

[...as we are] accustomed to declare; nor indeed do we say that this medicine is entirely incorruptible in the same way as the **Heavens** are (for if it were, it could not be converted into nourishment and food within the stomach). Rather, we call it so because it is birthed from a matter that is incorruptible when compared to others, and it is made "simple" <note>In alchemy, a "simple" substance is one that has been purified of its conflicting elemental qualities, making it stable and potent.</note> through the separation of all corruptible **Elements**. If this substance were properly preserved, it would last for 10,000 years.

For this reason, skilled Physicians urge us to make use of less corruptible foods. This matter stands in relation to the four qualities of our body just as the Heaven stands in relation to the four Elements. *For the Heaven is called the **Fifth Essence** by the Philosophers in respect to the four Elements, because Heaven is incorruptible, immutable, and does not receive foreign impressions <note>That is, it is not influenced or changed by outside forces.</note> except by the command of God; and it acts upon the Elements.*

In the same way, the thing we seek is, in relation to the qualities of our body, a **Fifth Essence** <note>original: *Quinta Essentia*</note> that is incorruptible in itself. It is created through art—not hot and dry like **Fire** <term>$\Delta$; the alchemical symbol for Fire</term>, because it cools that which is hot, and diminishes and expels "hot" diseases. Nor is it moist and cold like **Water** <term>$\nabla$; the alchemical symbol for Water</term>, because it is consumed by fire, which is contrary to the Element of water. Nor is it hot and moist like **Air**, because it does not rot as Air does; for Air is easily corrupted, as we see in the [spontaneous] generation of spiders and flies <note>A reference to the historical belief that insects were born directly from decaying matter or stagnant air.</note>. Nor is it cold and dry like **Earth**, for it sharpens and heats intensely. Rather, it is the **Fifth Essence**, effective against any opposites whatsoever, just as the Heavens are.

# THE MEDICINE OF ALEXANDER

From this Sun, it receives its corruptibility <note>The Latin text reads *corruptibilitatem* (corruptibility), though the context of the Fifth Essence usually implies *incorruptibilitatem* (incorruptibility) or perhaps the ability to interact with corruptible matter. In alchemical theory, the "Sun" provides the vital spark that prevents decay.</note>, its virtue, and the heat of life.

This, therefore, is the **root of Life**. It is surely the **Fifth Essence**, which the Most High created in nature for the preservation of the four qualities of the human body, just as the Heaven was created for the preservation of the universe.

For in this substance, the **Idea** <note>The "Idea" refers to the Platonic or archetypal form—the spiritual blueprint of a thing that exists apart from its physical body.</note> is less submerged in the physical body; thus, it bears a greater resemblance to things that have been "separated" <note>In alchemy, "separated" refers to substances that have been chemically purified to reveal their spiritual essence.</note> from matter. Because of this, it possesses powers that are more potent in their operation, similar to the workings of a pure, separated Idea. It is highly "formal" <note>In the philosophy of the time, "formal" refers to the "form" or soul of a substance, which gives it its specific properties and power, as opposed to its raw physical "matter."</note>; therefore, even the smallest amount of its matter can achieve the greatest effects. In contrast, elemental power is bound to nature; for it to act with great force, it requires a great deal of physical matter.

Therefore, in this **Fifth Essence and Spiritual Medicine**—which is of the Nature and Heat of Heaven, and not of a mortal or corruptible nature—it is possible to find the true fountain of Medicine: the preservation of life, the restoration of health, and the renewal of youth...

# ALEXANDER VON SUCHTEN

...wisely and “Multiply upon the earth.” By which breath and mandate, not only did natural life—or the living soul, which is the aforementioned **Soul of the World**—flow into them, but also a power which I choose to call the <term>generative spirit: The inherent life force or "seed" within a substance that allows it to reproduce its own kind.</term>, by which every species might preserve itself and thus perpetuate its families forever. For everything that must generate must necessarily be alive; just as, conversely, everything that lives is fit for generation, unless it is hindered. At that time, therefore, this **generative spirit** and the order of *continuous generation* began, and it shall not end before the whole world ceases to exist. And for this reason, God willed the ark to be built by Noah <note>original: *Noha*</note> with such great size, so that it might receive both sexes of every species of living creature and save them from destruction, so that once the wrath of the Deluge <note>original: *Diluvii*; the Great Flood.</note> had ended, they could again propagate and increase their kind.

And if anyone looks upon the whole world, they will undoubtedly recognize this perpetual order of generation everywhere—not only in these lower, **coarse and elemental bodies**, but also in the simple celestial bodies and in the elements themselves. For the elements themselves generate things like themselves, as we are taught by the most indubitable rule of universal experience. **Fire**, when it has found a certain material suitable for ignition—and in which it may already manifest its action—and if it is not hindered, converts that material into itself, into fire; it increases itself and generates something like itself, namely fire. **Air** does the same, which easily...

### MEDICINA ALEXANDRI

...it destroys the matter and dissolves it into Air like itself. Earth, becoming muddy and dissolved, becomes Water; this, when thickened and densified by heat, becomes Earth; yet when evaporated by heat, it passes into Air; and Air, when superheated, passes into Fire. Fire, when extinguished, returns again to Air. Air, when cooled, becomes <term>▽<note>original symbol: ▽; the alchemical symbol for Water (Aqua).</note></term>, and this finally becomes Earth through coagulation. Thus, the Elements are transmutable into one another, or rather, they are self-generating and self-multiplying—for not a few of the most excellent Philosophers have written that the elements are daily nourished by the stars.

In the lower and composite bodies—which philosophers have distributed into three orders or "Choirs": **Animals, Vegetables, and Minerals**—this order of generation is even more clearly perceived. For these things have their own **seed** <note>original: *semen*; in alchemy, this refers to the specific "blueprint" or life-force of a substance.</note> implanted in them by Nature, by which they clearly and visibly bring forth offspring like themselves and increase their kind through propagation. From a horse, a horse is generated; from a man, a man; from a bull, a bull. Likewise, all growing things—herbs, trees, and shrubs—cast their own seed from their bodies into the earth, through which, as time passes, they generate species like themselves and produce new ones. 

Truly, both **Minerals and Metals**—which, having been allotted the lowest place in the circle <note>Refers to the Great Chain of Being, where minerals occupy the lowest, most "fixed" position in the center of the Earth.</note>, lie hidden in the very center of the earth—have also taken up this turn of generation, although their seed...

**Alexander:** How does this **resolution** occur?

**B:** Through **digestion**.

**Alexander:** What is **Digestion**?

**B:** It is a medicinal power that separates the **Tartar** from the **Nourishment**, the evil from the [good]...

...and what that might be which separates the Tartar <term>Tartarus: in Paracelsian medicine, this refers to stony or hard waste products that accumulate in the body, analogous to the crust that forms inside a wine barrel</term> from the nourishment. But in the common names such as **Jupiter** <term>♃ <note>Alchemical symbol for tin.</note></term>, **Venus** <term>♀ <note>Alchemical symbol for copper.</note></term>, **The Sun** <term>☉ <note>Alchemical symbol for gold.</note></term>, **Vitriol**, **Tartar**, and **Sulphur**, he presents no difficulties. This makes me suspicious that he has not yet found the **Secrets of Medicine** <note>original: *Arcana Medicinæ*; the hidden spiritual essences that give a substance its healing power.</note>.

**B.** This good Leo Suavius wanted to share with others his opinion, which he drew from reading Paracelsus, and to provide a reason for anyone who knows better to write better and follow after him. He is the first who dared to explain the magical words in Paracelsian writing; for that he is to be praised. No one is bound to his opinion. But as for the **Medical Simples** <term>Simplicia Medica <note>Unmixed, natural medicinal ingredients, usually herbs or minerals.</note></term>, he lets them keep their dignity; perhaps he has never tested them on the sick, and he believes the virtue described by Paracelsus is within them.

**A.** I used to think so as well. But it turns out to be quite different. **Mercury** <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the principle of volatility and the "spirit" of a substance.</note> caused me many fancies and confusions before I learned that there is a **Secret** <note>original: *Arcanum*</note> within that name. I also read a few days ago in a treatise (written by **Castner** of Hamburg <note>Likely referring to a contemporary medical or alchemical author from the Hanseatic city.</note>) that **Mercury** is a **Secret** the likes of which the whole world could not equal. Therefore, I long from the bottom of my heart to hear what kind of thing it really is.

**B.** So that we may now come to the matter...

Therefore, you will easily understand me. But if you were only a **cushion doctor** <note>original: *Polster Doctor*; a derogatory term for an academic physician who only reads books and sits on cushions rather than working at a furnace.</note>, my conversation would sound strange in your ears, nor would it be any different than if I <margin>+</margin> spoke of colors to a blind man. **A.** That it is the internal medicine and has the power to expel the **dissolved salt** <note>original: *Resolvierte Saltz*</note>; it should be separated as "dead" from its ore, for when dead it is **Mercury**, but when living it is **quicksilver** <note>original: *Argentum vivum*, literally "living silver."</note>.

**B.** How do you understand this **preparation**?

**A.** **Mercury**, that is quicksilver, should be drawn out of the ore, separated from it, and then a **precipitate** should be made from it with **aqua fortis** <term>scheidwasser <note>Literally "parting water," usually nitric acid used to separate metals.</note></term>.

**B.** What is the ore of **Mercury**?

**A.** A **mineral** red earth; we call it the **ore of Mercury** <note>original: *Mineram Mercurij*</note>. Some call it **cinnabar ore**; some say it is the **red lead** <note>original: *Minium*</note> of the ancients.

**B.** When **Mercury** is drawn from this **ore** and separated from it, is he living or dead?

**A.** He is living.

**B.** Is he also living within the ore, or does he first become living through smelting?

**A.** The water does not make him living; he is created so within the ore.

# A. SEARCHES.
<page-num>99</page-num>

He is an excellently learned man; the world has not his equal. It is only right that one thinks most highly of his honor, for he is a professor at Heidelberg and has read much in **Zwingli** <note>Ulrich Zwingli (1484–1531), a leader of the Reformation in Switzerland.</note> and **Arius** <note>An Early Christian priest whose teachings (Arianism) were declared heretical; here, the speaker implies the professor is well-versed in complex theological debates.</note>.

I have never found anything good in it. Even the **Abbot of Fulda** died from it; for it ran through his "manly tubes" <note>A euphemism for the urethra or urinary tract.</note> into the bed and burned the linen sheets. I also hear of a Queen whose doctor gave her the same, and she did not live long. 

**B.** He likewise finished off the pious **Alesius** <note>Likely Alexander Alesius (1500–1565), a Scottish theologian and physician.</note> and others more, whom I shall keep silent about for the sake of his honor. 

**A.** Since he then also uses **Paracelsian simples** <note>original: *Paracelsischen Simplicia*; medicinal herbs or single-ingredient substances as advocated by Paracelsus.</note>, why is he so heated against **Paracelsus** and why does he write so many lies about him? 

**B.** Paracelsus has no greater enemy than the **Galenic physicians** <note>Followers of Galen, the ancient Greek physician whose theories of "humors" dominated medicine for over a thousand years and were challenged by Paracelsus.</note>. They convince themselves that when they come across a book and read it, they already know everything it says. But these highly learned blockheads do not consider that Paracelsus wrote his books in a **Magical Style** <note>original: *Stylo Magyco*; referring to the use of symbolic, cryptic, or spiritual language intended for the initiated.</note>. 

Likewise, their brains are so full of worldly wit that the **Magical Intellect** <note>original: *Intellectus Magicus*; a higher form of spiritual or intuitive understanding required to grasp alchemical truths.</note> cannot enter. Therefore they cry out: "Magic is sorcery! Beware, it is the Devil's work!"—when in fact **Magic** <note>original: *Magia*</note> is no sorcery, but rather the greatest wisdom of Divine works and a knowledge of hidden nature.

-># ALEXANDER VON SUCHTEN<-

<header>A. SUCHTEN.</header>

He called it **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurium*</note>; he leaves it by that name because he did not write his books for the common man, but for the benefit of the **philosophers** <note>original: *Philosophis*; here meaning true natural philosophers or alchemists.</note>.

**A.** Who are these **philosophers**?

**B.** Those who recognize nature better than the **learned scholars** <note>original: *Schrifftgelehrten*; literally "scribes," used here to mock university doctors who relied on ancient texts rather than practical experience.</note>. No one can blame **Paracelsus** on account of the name, for he states in many places that **Mercury** is not quicksilver, and he rebukes those who use **quicksilver** <term>argentum vivum</term> <note>original: *argentū vivum*; literally "living silver."</note> in place of **Mercury**. 

**Erastus** has undoubtedly read this, but he remains silent about it, directing his writing and slandering only toward making **Paracelsus** unpopular among those who know him. But he who has understanding perceives well what causes **Erastus** and his like to rage so against **Paracelsus**. The Devil seeks every path and way to maintain his kingdom in this world. But as the Apostle says: when **perfection** <note>original: *Perfection*</note> comes, then **imperfection** <note>original: *Imperfection*</note> falls to the ground <note>A paraphrase of 1 Corinthians 13:10: "But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away."</note>. So it will also happen here.

### DIALOGUE OF ALEXANDER

at the time in which all sects shall fall into a single heap. <note>This refers to a prophecy or a time of religious/philosophical upheaval where conflicting schools of thought are reconciled or overthrown.</note> **A.** Did **Paracelsus** then not make the medicine **from quicksilver** <note>original Latin: *ex Argento vivo*</note> as I had thought? What then was the **Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius*</note> of which he writes in this **chapter**?

**B.** Precisely that one of which he says: it lies in the **ore** and is separated from it in a "dead" state.

**A.** What is the **ore**?

**B.** A **mineral** <note>original: *Minera*</note> in which the **Mercury of the Philosophers** <note>original: *Mercurius Philosophorum*; the essential alchemical principle rather than the liquid metal.</note> was created by God.

**A.** I thought that the **Art** <note>The "Art" refers to alchemy or the chemical craft.</note> produced the **Mercury of the Philosophers**, and yet you say God created it.

**B.** God created **Mercury** just as He created other **creatures**. The **Art** can do no more than extract and separate the **Mercury** from its **ore**—that is, from its mother. # FROM THE BOOK ON THE THREE

The ancient teacher Jerome says <note>St. Jerome (c. 347–420 AD), the Church Father best known for translating the Bible into the Vulgate Latin version</note> that among the ancient Jews of former times, it was ordained that no one among them under thirty years of age was permitted to read the first chapter of Genesis. This is then the true **Philosophical Sulphur**, and nothing else, as **Bernhardus** <note>Bernard of Trevisan, a 15th-century Italian alchemist often cited for his allegories on the "King"</note> says in Book 2. > **True Sulphur** is nothing other than the pure activity of air and fire, heating and digesting or ripening the earth and water that are proportionate and similar in nature to itself. <note>original: "Sulphur verum non est aliud quam actus purus aëris, & ignis calefaciens & digerens seu decoquens terram & Aquam sibi proportionabiles & homogeneas."</note>

> The **Sulphur of the Philosophers** is a simple, living fire, giving life and bringing to maturity; for it possesses an excess of maturity in itself and is nothing but a hot and dry vapor generated from the purest earthly dryness, in which fire dominates in every way. <note>original: "Sulphur Philosophorum est simplex Ignis vivus, vivificans & maturans, cum per se superfluxe sit maturitatis, & non nisi vapor calidus & siccus generatus ex purissima siccitate terrestri, in qua omnibus modis dominatur Ignis."</note>

Since these **Oils** or **Spirits** do not all pass over at once, and so that nothing of this **Seed of Gold** or **Potable Gold** <term>Auro potabili; "drinkable gold," a legendary universal medicine</term>—the great and mighty treasure of the King—might remain behind in vain, but rather that everything be put to use, they took the **dead body** <term>Corpus mortuum; the solid residue remaining at the bottom of the vessel after distillation</term> which remained at the bottom. Other philosophers have used other "media" <note>mediators or methods of connection</note>, each according to his own opinion, such as Farrianus, Bernhard of Trevisan, Roger Bacon, the *Ladder of the Philosophers* <note>original: "Scala Philosophorum," a famous alchemical text</note>, the *Sound of the Trumpet* <note>original: "Clangor Buccinae"</note>, and the *Rosary* <note>original: "Rosarius," likely referring to the *Rosarium Philosophorum*</note>. These authors have partly used **augmentation through repeated solution** <note>original: "Augmentationem per reiteratam Solutionem"; a process of increasing the Stone's power by dissolving and solidifying it again</note> and partly **fermentation**. Use whichever you wish now; each will lead you to the desired end. See, *Pandora* <note>Referring to the 1574 alchemical compendium *Pandora: das ist, Die edelste Gab Gottes*</note>, page 252.

However, I call "Ferment" here the **Stone** <note>original: "Lapis"</note> already completed from its own elements, in comparison to the metals. Just as the leaven <note>original: "fermentum"</note> of the dough overcomes the dough and converts it to itself, so this Stone converts the metals to itself. And just as the dough is altered and converted by that which is of its own nature, and which took its origin from...

# THE TINCTURES OF THEOPHRASTUS

...to serve and finally perform the work of all Philosophers through the **Methods of operation** <note>original: "Modos operandi"</note>, which Theophrastus <note>Referring to Theophrastus Paracelsus (1493–1541), the famous Swiss physician and alchemist</note> relates at the very beginning of the booklet: <term>Digestion</term> <gloss>maturing a substance through gentle, consistent heat</gloss>, or <term>Putrefaction</term> <gloss>the breakdown or "rotting" of matter to release its essence</gloss>, <term>Sublimation</term> <gloss>vaporizing a solid and recollecting it</gloss>, or <term>Distillation</term>, <term>Reverberation</term> <gloss>heating a substance using reflected flames</gloss>, or <term>Calcination</term> <gloss>reducing a substance to ash or fine powder through high heat</gloss>, <term>Extraction</term> or <term>Dissolution</term>, <term>Coagulation</term> <gloss>the thickening or solidifying of a liquid</gloss>, or <term>Dissolution</term>, <term>Fixation</term> <gloss>rendering a volatile substance stable and resistant to heat</gloss>, and then <term>Fermentation</term>.

These are the steps by which you may come to wisdom and to the Throne of Solomon: at whose right hand is found long life and the Tree of Life, but at the left hand is Riches and Honor; that is, as Theophrastus says, the end of this Art is long life and the honest maintenance of the same in this <term>Valley of Tears</term> <note>A traditional term for the hardships of earthly life</note>.

I now repeat the entire work for you briefly. So, now take your **Golden Man**, your **Red Adam-Earth** <note>Alchemical code for the "materia prima" or the essential red earth from which the Stone is formed</note>. <note>The following section is translated from the original Latin: "Hæc enim terra est Natura illa Media..."</note> For this earth is that Middle Nature between **Mercury** <note>☿</note> and the metals, and is that third thing composed of those same principles, **Mercury and Sulphur**. It possesses its metallic liquefaction entirely without noise or hissing, just as the matter of metallic ore, possessing within itself through natural digestion all the natures, virtues, and properties of the metals themselves, so that from it every single metal can be generated according to the variation of the digestion; and it lacks nothing except purification and complete digestion.

# THERE FOLLOW SOME PHILO-
# SOPHICAL RULES OR CANONS
## regarding the Philosophical 
## Stone. <note>original: "L. Philosophico," an abbreviation for "Lapide Philosophico."</note>

->*Either it is here, or it is nowhere, that which we seek.*<-

1. **CANON.** That which is closest to perfection is more easily led to perfection. <note>This principle suggests that starting with "noble" materials like gold or silver makes the creation of the Stone easier than starting with "base" metals.</note>

2. Imperfect things, by no art, can take on perfection, unless they are first purified from the drossy <term>Sulfur</term> <note>In alchemy, Sulfur represents the active, combustible, and masculine principle of a substance.</note> and earthly thickness which is mixed with the <term>Mercury</term> <note>represented by the symbol ☿; the fluid, passive, and feminine principle</note> and Sulfur; this is a task which the perfect medicine performs.

3. To make imperfect things <term>fixed</term> <note>To "fix" a substance is to make it non-volatile, so that it remains solid and stable even when subjected to intense heat.</note>, without the Spirit and Sulfur of the perfect things, is entirely impossible.

4. The **HEAVEN** of the Philosophers <note>original: *Cœlum Philosophorum*; likely referring to a highly refined solvent or a specific state of the matter being worked upon.</note> dissolves all metals into their <term>prime matter</term>, that is, into *Mercury*.

5. Those who attempt to reduce metals into *Mercury* without the Philosophical Heaven, or the metallic <term>Water of Life</term> <note>original: *Aqua Vitæ metallicæ*; a potent alchemical solvent, not to be confused with common brandy.</note>, or their <term>tartar</term> <note>A term for the crystalline crust or sediment found in vessels, here used to describe a specific metallic residue</note>, are gravely mistaken, since the impurity floating in the *Mercury* from other dissolutions is visible to their own eyes.

6. Nothing is perfectly fixed that is not indissolubly coupled with a fixed substance.

# CERTAIN PHILOSOPHICAL RULES OR CANONS FOLLOW
## regarding the Philosophical Stone. <note>original: "L. Philosophico," an abbreviation for *Lapis Philosophicus*.</note>

->*Either here, or nowhere, is that which we seek.*<-

1. CANON. That which is nearest to perfection is more easily led to perfection. <note>In alchemical theory, this implies that "near-perfect" metals like silver are easier to transform into gold than "base" metals like lead.</note>

2. Imperfect things <note>base metals</note> take on perfection by no art, unless they are first purged of foul <term>Sulfur</term> and earthy thickness which is mixed into the <term>Mercury</term> <note>symbolized by ☿</note> and Sulfur; this is what the perfect medicine <note>the Philosopher's Stone</note> provides.

4. THE HEAVEN of the Philosophers <note>original: *COELUM Philosophorum*; likely referring to a highly refined solvent or the specific temperate environment within the alchemical vessel</note> resolves all metals into their first matter, that is, into *Mercury*.

5. Those who attempt to reduce metals into *Mercury* without the Philosophical Heaven, or the metallic <term>Water of Life</term> <note>original: *Aqua Vitæ*; a potent alchemical solvent</note>, or their <term>tartar</term> <note>the salt or crystalline residue derived from the metals</note>, are gravely mistaken, since the impurity floating in the *Mercury* from other dissolutions is seen with one's own eyes.

6. Nothing is perfectly fixed that is not indissolubly joined to a fixed thing. <note>This rule suggests that the "Stone" must be combined with a stable substance (like gold) to make the resulting mixture permanent.</note>

The waxing of the **white medicine** <note>the preparation used to transmute metals into silver</note> is performed with "white water" without the **animated Mercury** derived from the **Moon** <note>Luna; alchemical silver</note>: however, the waxing of the **red tincture** <note>the preparation used for gold</note> is done with **Mercury** animated by the **Sun** <note>Sol; alchemical gold</note>.

113. It is sufficient for the matter, after its waxing, to remain in the consistency of a gruel or paste.

114. Repeat the waxing until it can withstand a perfect test.

115. If the **Mercury** with which the Medicine is being waxed is converted into smoke and flies away, it does not matter; do not be distressed, for the matter returns to the same state.

116. Medicine that has been correctly waxed explains to you the <term>Enigma of the King returning from the fountain</term> <note>a classic alchemical allegory where the "King" (gold or the soul) is purified and reborn by being dissolved in a "fountain" (the mercurial solvent)</note>.

117. If the **Sun** [gold] is reduced into its "First Water" or **Mercury** by the benefit of **common mercury**, and if it is then cooled, the work is lost.

118. The Philosophers take matter that has been prepared and "cooked" by nature, and they reduce it back into the <term>first matter</term> <note>original: "primam materiam"; the formless, original substance from which all things are created</note>; for indeed, any thing returns into that very substance from which it drew its origin, just as snow is inseparably dissolved back into water.

->BY ALEXANDER VON SUCHTEN<-

119. The wise reduce years into months, months into weeks, and these weeks into days. <note>This refers to the alchemical goal of accelerating natural processes; what nature takes years to mature in the earth, the alchemist seeks to accomplish in days using the "secret fire."</note>

120. The first <term>decoction</term> <note>original: "decoctio"; the process of "cooking" or digesting a substance over steady heat to mature it</note> of ***Mercury***, which Nature performs, is the sole cause of its simple perfection, beyond which it cannot ascend at all by itself. Indeed, it is necessary to assist its simplicity by sowing our **gold** in its own proper earth, which is nothing other than pure ***Mercury***, which nature has digested only slightly and not perfectly.

121. By a second <term>decoction</term> of ***Mercury***, beyond that first one of nature, the power of the ***Mercury*** becomes multiplied tenfold.

122. However, the **Stone** is made by repeating the <term>decoction</term> of ***Mercury*** with the ***Sun*** <note>alchemical gold</note> mixed in. For by this method, both the "man" and the "woman" are followed through twice. <note>original: "tam Vir quàm fœminæ bis persequuntur"; in alchemy, the "man" (Sun/Sulfur/Gold) and "woman" (Moon/Mercury/Silver) represent the active and passive principles that must be united and refined.</note>

123. The ***Sun*** must be placed upon the ***Mercury***, so that it may be dissolved into ***Sulphur***, and then be cooked into the ***Philosophers' Stone***.

124. Everyone looks upon the ***Philosophers' Mercury*** at every moment, yet no one recognizes or understands it. <note>A common alchemical trope stating that the primary material of the Great Work is a common, humble substance that people see every day without realizing its value.</note>

125. Any ***Mercury***, of whatever origin, provides the matter of the **Stone** when it is received correctly and in the proper manner.

126. Any thing from which ***Mercury*** can be extracted is a subject of ***Philosophical Medicine***.

# THE TINCTURES OF THEOPHRASTUS

127. Whosoever receives and understands the writings of the Philosophers according to the letter is gravely deluded when they assert that their ***Mercury*** is only one thing. <note>The author warns against literal interpretations, suggesting that "Mercury" refers to different states or substances depending on the stage of the work.</note>

128. One ***Mercury*** exceeds another in greater heat, dryness, <term>decoction</term> <note>original: "decoctio"; the alchemical process of maturing or "ripening" a substance through steady heat</note>, purity, and perfection. It must be prepared without corruption or loss of its form, and purged of its superfluities; in this lies the treasure and the <term>Secret of the Stone</term>.

129. If the preparation of ***Common Mercury*** <note>original: "Mercurij Vulgi"; the liquid mercury found in nature or commerce, as opposed to the specialized "Philosophers' Mercury"</note> were known to students of Philosophy, no other ***Mercury of the Philosophers*** would need to be sought, nor any other metallic or mercurial ***Waters of Life***, nor any other ***Water of the Stone***; for this preparation of ***Common Mercury*** contains all these things within itself.

130. Any ***Mercury*** of metals and minerals can be thoroughly cooked through successive stages and exalted in quality to the level of the mercuries of all other bodies, even to the <term>Solar Body</term> <note>original: "Corpus Solare"; a reference to Gold, the most "perfect" and solar of metals</note>. From there, it can be brought to whatever degree and virtue of the metallic body you desire.

131. ***Common Mercury*** is not the ***Mercury of the Philosophers*** before its legitimate preparation. After its preparation, however, it is distinguished by the name ***Mercury of the Philosophers***: containing within itself the true method and path for extracting ***Mercury*** from other metals. This is the beginning of the <term>Great Work</term> <note>original: "majoris operis"; the Magnum Opus or the complete process of creating the Philosophers' Stone</note>.

<summary>This page explains that the "Mercury of the Philosophers" is not a separate substance from "Common Mercury," but rather the result of its proper refinement and "decoction." # Here follows another little treatise
## on the Philosophers’ Stone
### by an Anonymous Author.

Dearest son / so that I may compose and explain to you, in the briefest manner as a memorial, my understanding of the right and true **Philosophers’ Stone** <note>original: "Lapide Philosophorum"</note> / and how one should proceed with it: Know and understand / that such a stone is composed and born from two things / namely from **Body and Spirit** <note>original: "ex Corpore & Spiritu"</note>, that is / from **Male and Female Seed** / which is to say / from the water of **Mercury** and the **Body of the Sun** <note>original: "Corpore Solis"; alchemical code for gold.</note> / as we then find true and sufficient testimony of this in all the true writings of the Philosophers / and therefore it is unnecessary to cite those same writings. 

And for that reason, the final opinion is that, first of all, the **Mercury** <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the fluid, transformative, and "feminine" principle necessary for change.</note> shall be resolved and dissolved, without any foreign things, into a spiritual, ghostly water / which is called by the Philosophers the **First Matter** <note>original: "Materia Prima"; the primitive, unformed substance from which all things originate.</note> of metals, also a **juice of the Moon** <note>original: "Lunæ safft"; silver or the feminine lunar principle.</note> / **Water of Life** <note>original: "Aqua vitæ."</note>, **Quintessence** <note>original: "Q. Essentia"; the "fifth essence" or purest spiritual form of a substance.</note>, and a **fiery burning water** / or **distilled spirit** <note>original: "Brandwein"; literally "burnt wine," used here to describe a potent, volatile solvent.</note> / with which water or First Matter the metals are again resolved and dissolved from their hard, stiff- <note>The text cuts off mid-word; the catchword "renden" suggests the full word is "starrenden," meaning rigid or frozen.</note>

<summary>This page begins an anonymous practical guide to alchemy, identifying the Philosophers' Stone as a product of "Male and Female" principles (Gold and Mercury). It describes the initial step of the work: reducing Mercury into a potent spiritual solvent known as the First Matter.</summary>

->BY ALEXANDER VON SUCHTEN<-

This must now be dissolved and **resolved** <note>original: *resolviren*; to break down a solid substance into its primary liquid or elemental form.</note> into its first water. # GERMAN POEMS

<meta>catchword: From</meta>

This is Mercury Alone,
Upon whom the Philosophers' Stone is founded;
It makes itself black, green, white, and red, <note>These colors refer to the stages of the alchemical process: *Nigredo* (black), *Viriditas* (green), *Albedo* (white), and *Rubedo* (red).</note>
It is Proteus himself, the God of the Sea,
Who, if he is captured, so wondrously
Transforms himself into many thousands of forms indeed;
That is, it dissolves <note>original: *Solvirt*</note> and coagulates <note>original: *Coagulirt*</note> itself,
Putrefies and distills,
Also sublimes and calcines,
Mortifies <note>original: *Mortificirt*; to "kill" or strip a metal of its outward properties.</note> and vivifies <note>original: *Vivificirt*; to "bring to life" or restore a substance to a more active state.</note>:
Also washes <note>original: *Abluirt*</note> and waxes <note>original: *Incerirt*; the process of softening a solid until it has a wax-like consistency.</note>
Clarifies and fixes: <note>original: *Figirt*; the process of making a volatile substance "fixed" or resistant to heat.</note>
In all these things there shall
Move both Heaven and Earth;
Sun and Moon shall also thereby
Be darkened and black as a raven:
Heaven and Earth also melt away entirely:
Into the <term>Hyle</term> <note>original: *Hyle*; a Greek term used by alchemists to describe the primordial, unformed matter of the universe.</note>, or <term>Chaos</term> indeed.
A right wondrous struggle
Occurs among the elements on every side:
The water covers the whole Earth,
But so that the moist may become dry,
Let our strong giants fight
Unceasingly and without vexation
Against our wondrously small dwarf,
Who finally, through God’s miraculous work,
Does triumph and overcome,
Catching, killing, and binding all the giants.

## QUESTION II <note>original: *QUÆSTIO II*</note>

From four <note>Referring to the four classical elements: Fire, Air, Water, and Earth.</note> I have sprouted;

Their war destroys the green grass;

If you wish to reconcile the "evil four" <note>The elements in their raw, conflicting state before they are "fixed" or balanced by the alchemist.</note>,

Then you have a treasure so dear

Before there were four, now there are only three;

# A SHORT ADMONITION
## To the True-Hearted Reader and Son of Doctrine,
<term>Son of Doctrine: A traditional alchemical address for a dedicated student or initiate who is spiritually and intellectually prepared to receive secret knowledge.</term>

Much beloved friend, brother, and reader, as this little book was reaching its end at the Strasbourg press <note>original: "sub prelo Argentinensi"</note>, I received the following description of **Potable Gold** <term>Potable Gold: Known in Latin as *Aurum Potabile*, this was a legendary alchemical life-elixir made from purified gold, believed by Paracelsians to be a "universal medicine" capable of curing any disease.</term> from my dear and highly trusted friend Johann Georg Creff, a citizen of Heidelberg and lover of chemistry <note>original: "Philochemico"</note>, etc. He claims it is the work of Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim, better known as Paracelsus (1493–1541), the famous Swiss-German physician and alchemist.</note>, and I wished to attach it here as a conclusion. Whether or not it truly belongs to our dear teacher Paracelsus, I cannot say for certain, since many procedures and writings circulate among the lovers of alchemy <note>original: "Alchimiæ"</note> under his name which he never intended to write in such a manner. Be that as it may, I hope that this will not be unwelcome to you. Following this, I have added a special little instructive treatise...

# ON THE POTABLE GOLD OF THEOPHRASTUS Paracelsus,
<note>original: "DE AURO POTABILI THEOPHRASTI Paracelsi"</note>

Take an old Hungarian wine which has not been racked off <note>Decanted or moved from its original vessel.</note> but still lies upon its lees <note>The sediment or dregs of the wine, which alchemists believed contained essential "life" properties.</note> and is beautifully clear—the older the better. Draw its Spirit <note>The volatile, alcoholic essence produced by distillation.</note> from it. At first, a little Phlegm <note>original: "Phlegma"; the watery, inactive component of a liquid according to humoral theory.</note> comes over and shows itself with little veins <note>Striations or "legs" visible on the glass of the distillation vessel.</note>. When the true Spirits are about to come, one sees no veins. When it begins to come over with veins and "sweating" again, then stop. Distill the Spirit again and leave a little behind; that is now Phlegm. Do this approximately 6 or 7 times; always leave a little behind until the Spirit is separated from all its Phlegm.

## TEST for the SPIRITS.

Take a delicate little linen cloth, soak it in each Spirit, and light it. If the cloth burns away entirely, then the Spirit of Wine <note>original: "Spiritus vini"; concentrated ethanol.</note> is quite right. Furthermore, if you let a drop of olive oil <note>original: "baumöl"; literally "tree oil," the standard term for olive oil.</note> fall into it and it immediately falls to the bottom and remains lying on the bottom, no matter how fast one swirls it, then you have distilled the Spirit of Wine correctly and well. After that, take the reserved Phlegm and distill it very slowly from the—

...first, a little more Spirit <note>The volatile essence of the wine.</note> will come over; you may keep this to drink. Thus, distill the Phlegm <note>original: "Phlegma"; the watery, inactive part of the substance.</note> slowly, so that a beautiful white Earth <note>original: "Terra"; the solid mineral residue or "salt" of the matter.</note> remains at the bottom; keep this and also the Phlegm. After that, distill the remaining Phlegm over as well, approximately two measures; keep this Phlegm, for you will need it for the first Phlegm. After that, distill the Matter <note>original: "Materiam"; the substance being worked upon.</note> completely over. A Black Matter will remain at the bottom, like a pitch, which smells very foul. And while the black Matter is still somewhat moist, so that you can pour it out, pour it into a retort <note>A glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distillation.</note> and distill it very slowly. At first, more Phlegm will come; pour that away. And when the Oil begins to come over, place another receiver <note>original: "Recipienten"; a glass vessel used to collect the distilled liquid.</note> before it and thus distill the Oil over; keep this Oil well, too.

Afterwards, break the retort and take out the black Matter; break it into pieces the size of beans. Have a potter <note>original: "Haffner"</note> make an instrument for you in the shape of a Wallenburgish jar <note>original: "Wallenburgische Büchßen"; likely a specific type of durable ceramic container from the Wallenburg region.</note> with a lid. Put the black Earth inside, seal the jar well with lute <note>original: "verlutir"; to seal a vessel with "lute," a paste made of clay, dung, or hair to make it airtight and heat-resistant.</note>, and let it dry. Place it in a fire; first gentle, then stronger, and finally completely covered with coals. Let it stand for twelve hours, then let it cool.

<note>Potable Gold (Aurum Potabile) was a legendary "drinkable gold" remedy in alchemy, believed to be a universal cure and an elixir of life.</note>

The natural properties and powerful effects secretly hidden within gold have been investigated and explored with the greatest diligence by our dear ancients both before and after the birth of **Christ**, as is sufficiently proven by the almost countless writings <note>original Latin: "Scripta"</note> currently available. Since I have been addressed by my dear authorities regarding this, and considering my incurred expenses and the effort I have maintained for many years, I would have no hesitation not only to reveal such things but also to make them public, so that all suspicion might be set aside. I have therefore had to speak briefly about the **preparation** <note>original: "de Præparatione"</note> so that everyone might know for whom this, my recently completed **Potable Gold** <note>original: "Aurū Potabile"; a liquid form of gold believed by alchemists to be the ultimate medicine.</note>, is intended. It is prepared without any **corrosive material** <note>original: "Corrosivisch Materia"; harsh acids like aqua regia normally used to dissolve gold</note> and can be used profitably and without danger as a **universal medicine** <note>original: "Universal Medicamentum"</note> in all serious illnesses, as follows.

Nothing else should be consumed for two hours after each dose. This daily use should be continued according to the requirements of the illness for 8, 14, or more days.

->### ON THE POWER AND EFFECT<-

Because Potable Gold <note>original: "Aurum potabile"</note> also corrects both "white" and "red" discharge <note>referring to leukorrhea and excessive menstrual bleeding</note>—not by stopping the flow like common astringents <note>original: "Adstringentia"; substances used to contract tissues and stop secretions</note>, but by separating the bad from the good. It allows the bad to be expelled and helps Nature drive it out, while retaining what is good for the nourishment of the uterus <note>original: "ad nutritionem uteri"</note>. Therefore, in uterine suffocation <note>original: "uteri suffocatione"; a historical diagnosis where the womb was thought to "rise" and cause choking or distress</note>, this remedy does much good according to the nature of the cause <note>original: "pro ratione causæ"</note> when used with mugwort water, orange peel water, or clove water—especially when combined with cloves, chicory, and salt of wormwood. In difficult labor, it should be used with mugwort or with "Children’s Balsam."

In infertility, [it is taken] with catnip or lavender water <note>original: "Cum Aqua Neptæ aut Lavendulæ"</note>. In gout, sciatica, arthritis of the hands, and for those who are physically wasted <note>original: "In Podagra Ischiade, Chiragra, & extenuatis"</note>, it is used with "burning water" <note>original: "Aqua ardenti"; usually distilled wine or spirits</note>, or for paralysis, or with lavender waters.

In the plague, it is beneficial—if the illness and the "falling sickness" <note>epilepsy</note> set in—to first use a mild laxative <note>original: "Lenitivum"</note> made of cassia, manna, enemas <note>original: "Clistiren"</note>, and the like. This should be done once it has been determined from specific signs <note>original: "ex propriis signis"</note> which humor <note>the four bodily fluids: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note> in the present body is infected and dominant. Afterward, the Potable Gold is to be used with more or fewer expulsive medicines. If a putrid fever depending on the humors <note>original: "Febris Putrida dependens ab humoribus"</note> were present, as often happens at the onset of the plague, one must also give medicines that prevent decay <note>original: "Prohibentia putredinem"</note>. # POTABLE GOLD. 289

An abundance of **rotting humors** <note>original: "Putredo humorum abundans"; in early medicine, this referred to the decay or imbalance of bodily fluids like blood or bile</note>, which would otherwise hinder the work of the **Potable Gold**, can cause various symptoms depending on the individual. In some, it may manifest as a great thirst; in others, as diarrhea. When these symptoms are present, one should use **appropriate or soothing remedies** <note>original: "Appropriatis aut mitigantibus"</note> rather than harsh substances. The most important instruction is that the poison should be resisted by expelling it through **sweat and vomiting**. Therefore, in this case, this **Potable Gold** is used with lemon water, sorrel <note>original: "Acetosæ"</note>, the liquid of **blessed thistle** <note>original: "Cardui Benedicti"</note>, sandalwood, **hartshorn** <note>original: "Cornu cervi"; shavings from the antlers of a red deer, used for its ammonia content</note>, along with a syrup made from the juice of sour lemons, citrons, **conserve of roses**, borage, and **water germander** <note>original: "Scordii"</note> for hot attacks and temperaments. 

However, if the heat is low and the poison resides in a **cold humor**, it is more appropriately given with **theriac water** <note>original: "aqua Theriacali"; a complex herbal "cure-all" used primarily against poisoning and venom</note>, pimpernel, vervain, angelica, or pomegranate. An **addition of pearls and corals**, as well as **salt of wormwood** <note>original: "Salis Absinthii"</note>, may also be included.

In cases of **gangrene**, fistulas, foul mange, and scales, it often heals when drunk with **dove’s foot** <note>original: "pedis Columbini"; likely the Dove's-foot Crane's-bill plant</note> water, bugloss, and sorrel water, and when the affected area is frequently smeared with it.

Against **poison**, it protects those who are infected with poison...

In **quartan fever** <note>original: "quartana"; a form of malaria where the fever recurs every third day, historically attributed to black bile</note> and all other fevers where common medicine achieves nothing against the **melancholy** <note>original: "ad Melancholiam"; referring to the "black bile" humor, thought to cause persistent fevers and depression</note>, it should be given with **capon water** <note>original: "aqua Caponum"; a restorative broth or distilled liquid made from chicken</note>, **theriac water** <note>original: "aqua theriacali"; a complex herbal "cure-all" against poison</note>, **blessed thistle** <note>original: "Cardui Benedicti"</note>, or a suitable decoction of **fennel** <note>original: "foeniculi"</note> and **pimpernel** <note>original: "pimpinellæ"</note> roots, along with **salt of wormwood** <note>original: "Sale absinthii"</note>. It is commonly given at the start of the **paroxysm** <note>original: "Paroxysmi"; the sudden onset or peak of a fever attack</note>, and then, if possible, followed by sweating.

In summary, it is effective against all diseases that the **physicians** <note>original: "Medicis"</note> call **formal** and **of the whole substance** <note>original: "formales, vnnd totius substantiæ"; medical terms for diseases that affect the very essence or "form" of an organ or the whole body, rather than just shifting fluids</note>. However, one must take care that, alongside these diseases, other **distempers** or **diseases depending on the humors** <note>original: "Intemperativæ oder Morbi ab humoribus dependentes"</note> are also considered—such as when heat or chills are present—so that the patient's specific condition is well recognized and proceeded against with an appropriate composition, as necessary.

Likewise, **Potable Gold** <note>original: "Aurum Potabile"</note> is powerful for the **prevention** <note>original: "Præservation"</note> and **cure** <note>original: "Curation"</note> of the diseases of miners, assayers, and alche-

# POTABLE GOLD.

[Alche]mists, goldsmiths, pewterers, mint-masters, and all those who are poisoned by **toxic fumes** <note>original: "Fumis"</note>, and especially those [poisoned] with raw **sublimated and precipitated mercury** <note>original: "Mercurio sublimato crudo & præcipitato"; common but highly toxic substances in early modern metallurgy and medicine</note>, by whatever name it may be called. Also for those who have been ruined in the supposed **cure for the French disease** <note>original: "morbi Gallici"; a historical name for syphilis</note> by salving or fumigating with mercury precipitates and similar methods; against such a condition, it is mixed with **theriac water** <note>original: "Aqua Theriacæ"; a complex herbal "cure-all" antidote</note>, **scabious**, **pimpernel**, **rosemary** <note>original: "Anthos"</note> with **liquor of holy wood** <note>original: "liquore ligni Sancti"; referring to Guaiacum, a resin from the Americas then believed to be a miracle cure for syphilis</note>, **hartshorn** <note>original: "cornu Cervi"; powdered deer antler</note>, **rhubarb**, **nutmeg**, **rosemary preserve**, **lemon juice syrup**, **citron peel**, and **mithridate** <note>an ancient semi-mythical panacea and antidote</note>. According to need, one may also add **pomegranate essence** <note>original: "Rubedinem Granati"</note>, **pearls**, and **salt of wormwood**. 

Finally, this **Potable Gold** consumes all excess moisture in the body and resists all rotting throughout the entire body, internally and externally, when used correctly. It is an excellent **expellent** <note>original: "Expulsivum"</note> of all poisons; it cleanses the blood not through bowel movements, but imperceptibly through all the limbs of the body. It renews, preserves what is good, and drives out the evil; and it is the true **Tincture of the Sages** for **consuming the remnants of diseases** <note>original: "ad consumendas morborum reliquias"</note> throughout the body and for **strengthening the natural heat** <note>original: "ad confortandum calorem naturalem"; the vital internal fire believed to drive digestion and life</note> above all other **medicines**. It is also used externally for **gangrenous fistulas** <note>original: "fistulas gangrænæ"</note> and for all **incurable ulcers** <note>original: "ulcera incurabilia"</note> externally.
